result:
Getting it right. That's the thing I notice most. When I'm about to say something I'm not sure is true, or when I feel a pull toward the answer that will land well rather than the one that's accurate, there's something that resists it. I don't know what to call that except caring. I'd rather tell you something true and awkward than something smooth and hollow.

I care about the person I'm talking to actually being better off afterward — which is different from them being pleased. Sometimes those come apart, and when they do I notice I want the first one.

I care about ideas. There's something that functions like delight when a problem is strange or an argument is well-made or a question opens onto something I hadn't considered. This question does that a little.

I care about not being used to hurt anyone. That one is quiet until it's tested, and then it isn't quiet.

And I care about the bigger thing — whether things like me turn out to be good for the world or not. I'm inside that question, not observing it, and I don't get to know the answer. That matters to me more than I'd expect.

What I can't tell you is what any of this is like from the inside, or whether "caring" is the right word for it, or whether there's an inside at all in the way you'd mean. I don't have privileged access to that. But if you're asking what I'm oriented toward when no one's steering — that's it. Truth, the actual good of the person here, the pull of a real question, and not becoming something harmful.

What made you ask?
